subject: TowerBio marketplace pricing: SKU bundling effects on reseller netbacks & escrow cadence
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@towerbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TowerBio marketplace pricing: SKU bundling effects on reseller netbacks & escrow cadence

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for taking the walkthrough yesterday — appreciate the candidness on expected usage profiles across QA vs. production workloads. I pulled together a quick note on two items you flagged that will affect how we shape the private offer and channel math:

1) SKU bundling. If TowerBio folds the analytics agent (high-throughput) with the annotation seat SKU, the effective list price per token changes materially and will affect what resellers report as their netback. We've included a mocked sku_mapping_v1.xlsx in the Drive link for visibility.

2) Escrow / upfront credit cadence. You mentioned a preference for a 60-day escrow for early usage smoothing (to cover ramp). That will shift revenue recognition and typically reduces the visible upfront credit we can allocate to partners by ~4-6%.

Quick asks so we can finalize the PO draft (attached):
- Can procurement confirm whether bundles must be listed as a single SKU on AWS Marketplace (yes/no)? If yes, we should model netbacks differently.
- Ops: any constraints on invoicing cadence (monthly vs. true-up quarterly)?

If it's helpful I can loop in our finance ops lead with a short model that shows reseller netback delta for the two bundling options (separate SKUs vs. bundled).

Thanks —
Camila
Camila Reyes
Sr. Director, GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: TowerBio_AWS_PO_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Emma Liu <emma@towerbio.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TowerBio marketplace pricing: SKU bundling effects on reseller netbacks & escrow cadence

Camila —

Thanks for the summary and the draft. Quick answers:
- Procurement: we prefer bundles to be a single SKU in Marketplace for easier ordering from customers, but we can accept separate line items on our internal billing.
- Invoicing: TowerBio prefers monthly invoicing with a quarterly true-up (so monthly invoice, reconcile at quarter end).

Two follow-ups:
1) If bundling as single SKU reduces partner netbacks materially, can Redwood provide a pass-through schedule for the reseller so our partners (BioResell) see the commission waterfall? They asked us to provide visibility before committing to the rollout.
2) Escrow: 60 days is acceptable but can you confirm what that means for the visible discount in the private offer (we need a clean number for our legal and finance teams).

Cc'ing procurement@towerbio.com and ops@towerbio.com to keep them in the loop.

—Emma Liu
Director of Product, TowerBio
emma@towerbio.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: TowerBio marketplace pricing: SKU bundling effects on reseller netbacks & escrow cadence

Camila — forwarding edits from my side (see inline). Short version: we can support a single Marketplace SKU but the private-offer line items must include an internal mapping so that the reseller commission tier can be applied post-listing.

Inline notes:
- On bundling: modeling shows a ~5.2% reduction in reseller netback if the analytics agent's metered use is blended into the seat SKU without differentiated token tiers.
- On escrow: 60-day escrow reduces our up-front credit exposure; in practice the private offer visible discount will drop by 4 percentage points relative to a zero-escrow construct. We should bake that into the PO and call it out in the DocuSign memo.

Attached a sample DocuSign template we typically send — I left placeholders for the reseller waterfall and commit-level brackets.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: docsign_template_redwood.docx (DOCX stub)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@towerbio.com>, procurement@towerbio.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TowerBio marketplace pricing: SKU bundling effects on reseller netbacks & escrow cadence

Emma / Team —

Thanks for the clarity. I've updated the PO draft (attached) to:
- Map the bundled Marketplace SKU to three internal line items so resellers get a clear waterfall (see sku_mapping_v1.xlsx).
- Reflect a 4% reduction to the visible private-offer discount to account for the 60-day escrow cadence. We call this out in the DocuSign memo so accounting has visibility.
- Billing cadence set to monthly with quarterly true-up.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm the trivial change to the PO language in section 3.2 (we added the mapping clause). If you approve I will generate the DocuSign package.
2) Emma: if BioResell still requests a different commission treatment, we can provide a supplemental reseller agreement that sits behind the private offer (we'll need signed consent from TowerBio).

I'll prepare a short model (2 slides) showing reseller netback under "separate SKUs" vs "single bundle mapping" for your partner meeting next week.

Best,
Camila

Attachment: TowerBio_AWS_PO_Draft_v2.pdf, sku_mapping_v1.xlsx
